AutoloaderPanel.CalBowdenExpect:
• Filament loads until the extruder sensor triggers.
• Distance is saved per path.
• Values should be consistent across paths (within ~10 mm).
AutoloaderPanel.CalBowdenHint: Loads filament from the drive gear to the extruder sensor and records the distance. Run per path after encoder is calibrated.
AutoloaderPanel.CalBowdenWarn:
• Sensor never triggers → check extruder sensor wiring and pin polarity.
• Distance too short → filament may have buckled in the PTFE tube, check routing.
• Large variation between paths → PTFE tube lengths differ, check tube routing for each path.
AutoloaderPanel.CalDriveExpect:
• Filament moves forward ~100 mm.
• Measure the actual distance moved with calipers and enter it when prompted.
• Typical rotation_distance: 22–26.
AutoloaderPanel.CalDriveHint: Manually load filament through the drive gear. Marks a 100 mm reference, drives it, then prompts you to measure actual movement to calculate rotation_distance.
AutoloaderPanel.CalDriveWarn:
• No movement → engage the servo first (SA_ENGAGE), check the drive gear is clamped on the shaft.
• Filament slips → tighten the idler or increase servo_engaged_angle.
• Result far from 100 mm → re-check microsteps and full_steps_per_rotation settings.
AutoloaderPanel.CalEncSpeedExpect:
• Speed ramps up in steps.
• Stops when encoder falls behind.
• Saves max reliable speed — typically 100–200 mm/s.
AutoloaderPanel.CalEncSpeedHint: Ramps feed speed up until the encoder starts slipping, then saves the highest reliable speed. Run with filament loaded through the drive gear.
AutoloaderPanel.CalEncSpeedWarn:
• Saves very low speed (<50 mm/s) → check encoder wiring and position on the shaft.
• Fails immediately → encoder not counting, verify SA_ENCODER pin.
• Inconsistent results → ensure filament has no resistance in the tube.
AutoloaderPanel.CalEncoderExpect:
• Each path runs filament ~100 mm through the drive gear and compares encoder count to actual distance.
• Typical value: 0.010–0.020 mm/pulse.
AutoloaderPanel.CalEncoderHint: Measures mm of filament per encoder pulse. Run per path with filament loaded past the drive gear.
AutoloaderPanel.CalEncoderWarn:
• Value near 0 → encoder not counting, check wiring and SA_ENCODER pin.
• Values differ wildly between paths → filament not fully engaged, re-seat and retry.
• Value way off (>0.05) → wrong encoder resolution in sa_encoder config.
AutoloaderPanel.CalHomeExpect: • Selector moves toward endstop, slows, touches, backs off, then touches again to confirm position.
AutoloaderPanel.CalHomeHint: Moves the selector to the physical endstop and zeros its position. Required before any selector movement.
AutoloaderPanel.CalHomeWarn:
• Moves away from endstop → invert endstop pin or swap motor wires.
• Never triggers → check endstop wiring and SA_SELECTOR_STOP pin.
• Slams hard into the endstop → reduce selector_homing_speed in hardware.cfg.
AutoloaderPanel.CalMotorsExpect:
• Drive: first move pushes filament toward the toolhead (forward).
• Selector: first move travels away from the endstop toward higher path numbers.
• Both motors click/buzz and return to starting position.
AutoloaderPanel.CalMotorsHint: Run both buzz tests to confirm motor wiring and direction.
AutoloaderPanel.CalMotorsWarn:
• No movement → check motor wiring and driver power.
• Wrong direction → swap any two motor phase wires (or invert the direction_pin in config).
• Very weak → increase driver current in hardware.cfg.
AutoloaderPanel.CalSelectorExpect:
• Homes, sweeps outward until stall detected or end reached, then homes back.
• Reports total travel (~105–130 mm for 6 paths) and even spacing (~21 mm).
• Answer any on-screen prompts via the Response field that appears at the top of the panel.
AutoloaderPanel.CalSelectorHint: Sweeps the full rail using stallguard to find the far end, then homes back to measure total travel and calculate even path spacing.
AutoloaderPanel.CalSelectorWarn:
• Stalls mid-rail → increase selector_stall_threshold in hardware.cfg.
• Misses the far end → decrease selector_stall_threshold.
• Spacing is wrong → verify the rail is unobstructed and re-run.
